definition: to finish your studies and receive a degree from a school or college

collocations.example: Many students hope to graduate from college and find good jobs.
She worked hard to graduate with honors last year.

definition: the small, hard seeds of food plants such as wheat or rice

collocations.example: The country increased grain production to feed its people.
A poor harvest pushed grain prices higher this year.

definition: relating to visual art, drawing, or design

collocations.example: She studied graphic design at a well-known art school.
The museum displays many works from the graphic arts.

definition: to fully understand something, especially something difficult

New employees must fully grasp the safety rules.

definition: feeling thankful because someone has helped you

collocations.example: We are grateful for all your help this year.
I am deeply grateful to my mentor for her advice.

definition: a place in the ground where a dead body is buried

definition: the natural force that pulls objects down toward the earth

definition: to welcome someone with words or actions when you meet

definition: a firm, tight hold on something

definition: being the total amount before taxes or costs are taken out

definition: a rule or piece of advice about how to do something

Everyone should follow the guidelines when handling the chemicals.

definition: a musical instrument with strings that you play with your fingers

collocations.example: He learned to play the guitar as a teenager.

definition: a stop or pause in movement or activity

definition: an area of water near land where ships can stay safely

collocations.example: The town has a deep natural harbor for large ships.

definition: unpleasant, severe, and difficult to accept

They soon faced the harsh reality of running a business.

definition: something that could be dangerous or cause harm

definition: the main office where a company or group is controlled

The firm plans to move its headquarters abroad.

definition: to become healthy again, or to make a wound better

collocations.example: Small cuts usually heal quickly if kept clean.
The broken bone should heal completely within a month.

definition: the back part of the human foot, below the ankle

definition: for this reason; therefore

definition: the traditions, buildings, and culture passed down over many years

These old castles are part of our national heritage.

definition: to draw attention to something so that people notice it

The manager highlighted a problem with the new system.

definition: a main public road that connects towns and cities

collocations.example: Traffic moved slowly along the busy highway all morning.
They drove north along the highway for several hours.

definition: a small or indirect suggestion about something

collocations.example: He dropped a hint about the surprise party.

definition: the part of the body on each side where the leg meets the waist

definition: connected with God or religion; sacred

collocations.example: Many pilgrims travel to this holy place each year.
The priest blessed the holy water before the service.

definition: a strong feeling of fear and shock

definition: a person or group that invites and takes care of guests

collocations.example: She was a gracious host throughout the entire evening.
The exchange student lived with a kind host family.

definition: unfriendly and showing strong dislike or opposition

definition: all the people who live together in one house

She manages to run a large household alone.

definition: the quality of being funny, or the ability to find things funny

collocations.example: She has a great sense of humor and laughs easily.
His dry humor kept the whole office laughing.

definition: an idea suggested as an explanation but not yet proven

definition: being the best possible or exactly right for a purpose

definition: who someone is; the facts that show who a person is

definition: a set of beliefs and ideas, especially about politics

definition: a person who comes to live permanently in a new country

The city helps each new immigrant find work.

definition: relating to the body's natural ability to fight disease

definition: a strong effect that one thing has on another

definition: relating to an empire or its ruler

definition: to put a plan, system, or decision into action

Managers will implement several changes next month.

definition: to show that someone is involved in a crime or something wrong

definition: to suggest something is true without saying it directly

definition: to bring goods into a country from abroad to sell

definition: the quality of being important or mattering a great deal

They attach great importance to customer safety.

definition: to officially force a rule, tax, or limit on people

collocations.example: The government may impose a new tax on fuel.

definition: an opinion or feeling you have about someone or something

collocations.example: She made a good first impression at the interview.
He worked hard to make a strong impression.

definition: something that encourages a person to do something

Students had little incentive to study during summer.

definition: an event, especially an unusual or unpleasant one

Police are investigating a serious incident downtown.

definition: to include something as part of a larger thing

collocations.example: The company tries to incorporate feedback from its users.

definition: freedom from the control of other people or things

definition: not controlled by, or not needing help from, other people

definition: a number that shows changes in prices, values, or levels

definition: certain to happen and impossible to avoid

definition: a baby or very young child

The nurse carefully held the premature infant.

definition: to pass a disease to a person, animal, or plant

collocations.example: A single mosquito can infect many people with the virus.
Thousands of residents became infected during the outbreak.

definition: to fill something with air or gas so that it expands

collocations.example: He stopped to inflate a tire before the long trip.
Be sure to fully inflate the life jacket first.

definition: one of the foods or substances that something is made from

collocations.example: The active ingredient in this drug reduces pain.
Rice is the main ingredient in this dish.

definition: to live in a particular place

collocations.example: Few animals inhabit this dry, rocky region.
The small island is inhabited by rare birds.

definition: to receive money or property from someone after they die

definition: happening at the beginning; first

definition: to make something start, especially an important process

definition: to put liquid, especially medicine, into the body with a needle

collocations.example: Nurses inject the vaccine into the upper arm.

definition: to create new ideas, methods, or products

collocations.example: Successful companies must constantly innovate to stay ahead.
The team works to innovate and improve its products.

definition: ideas, advice, or information that you give to help something

collocations.example: Her valuable input improved the final report.
All team members provided input on the plan.

definition: to ask for information about something

collocations.example: She called the office to inquire about the job.
Officials will inquire into the cause of the accident.

definition: to put something inside or into something else

collocations.example: Please insert the card into the machine slowly.
You must insert a coin to start the machine.

definition: a clear and deep understanding of something

collocations.example: The book offers real insight into human behavior.
We hope to gain insight from the survey results.

definition: to make someone feel they want to do something good

collocations.example: Great teachers can inspire students to work harder.
Her success can inspire others to follow their dreams.

definition: to put equipment or software in place so it is ready to use

collocations.example: The company will install new software next week.

definition: a natural ability or feeling that makes you act without thinking

collocations.example: A mother's natural instinct is to protect her child.
Good managers learn to trust their instincts.

definition: an organization set up for research, education, or a special purpose

collocations.example: She works at a well-known research institute.

definition: a large, important organization such as a bank or university

collocations.example: The bank is a respected financial institution.
He teaches at a large academic institution.

definition: to combine things so that they work together as one

collocations.example: The firm will integrate the new team into the company.
It took months to fully integrate the two systems.

definition: relating to the ability to think, reason, and understand

collocations.example: The job requires strong intellectual ability and focus.
Her intellectual curiosity led her to read widely.

definition: the ability to learn, understand, and think clearly

collocations.example: Dolphins are well known for their high intelligence.
Solving the puzzle quickly is a sign of intelligence.

definition: to talk to or work together with other people

collocations.example: Children learn to interact with others at school.

definition: to get involved in something that is not your business

collocations.example: She never interferes in other people's affairs.

definition: the inside part of something such as a building or car

collocations.example: She studied interior design at college for three years.

definition: relating to the inside of something

collocations.example: The government manages its own internal affairs.

definition: involving two or more countries

collocations.example: The agreement should boost international trade between the nations.

definition: to explain or decide on the meaning of something

definition: to become involved in a situation to change what happens

collocations.example: The government may intervene in the dispute soon.

definition: close and private, involving a strong personal connection

collocations.example: They have a close, intimate relationship built on trust.

definition: the act of an army entering a country by force to take control

definition: to create or design something that did not exist before

collocations.example: He hoped to invent a machine to save water.

definition: to put money into something hoping to earn more later

collocations.example: Many people choose to invest in the stock market.
The firm invested heavily in new technology.

definition: saying the opposite of what you mean, often to be funny

definition: to keep one person or thing separate from others

definition: a place where criminals are kept as punishment

definition: a fast aircraft powered by jet engines

definition: shared by, or involving, two or more people or groups

collocations.example: The two firms formed a joint venture last year.

definition: a serious magazine containing articles about a particular subject

collocations.example: Her study appeared in a respected academic journal.
Researchers hope to publish in a top journal.

definition: a person who collects and writes news for the media

collocations.example: He is a respected freelance journalist in the city.

definition: a group of people who decide if someone is guilty in a court

definition: to give a good reason that shows something is right or fair

definition: a piece of paper or tag that gives information about something

definition: the natural features of an area of land that you can see

definition: the second of two people or things just mentioned

definition: the sound you make when you laugh

definition: to start something new or introduce a new product

collocations.example: The company will launch a new product next month.
